key_insight: Federated deep learning let two different cohorts jointly improve cardiovascular disease risk prediction without sharing patient-level data.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help healthcare organizations build stronger risk models across sites while better protecting privacy and data governance requirements.
method: Trained deep survival models using federated learning across Lifelines and the Rotterdam Study
Compared federated models with locally trained models
evidence_signal: Performance improved slightly with federation: Rotterdam Study C-statistic rose from 0.728 to 0.739, and Lifelines from 0.783 to 0.787.
watch_item: Results came from only two heterogeneous cohorts with different outcome definitions, so real-world deployment may require careful harmonization and validation.
paper_title: Federated Deep Learning for Privacy-Preserving Cardiovascular Disease Risk Prediction
